newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher after orderly rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher after orderly rally.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed sharply higher, as U.S. June economic data provided the springboard for a broad-based but orderly rally, traders and analysts said.
"Bonds are very resilient right now," one debt futures trader said. "The market is on the path of the most pain. Everyone has been trying to sell into these rallies."

T-bond futures led advances against Eurodollars, but several floor analysts attributed September T-bonds' momentum toward seven-month highs to the break of 6.50 percent in the 30-year cash T-bond yield.

The technical break of what was a solid support level, yield-wise, touched off heavy selling of two-year T-notes and buying of T-bonds, as fund and portfolio managers extended durations in the cash market, futures traders said.
Talk of a $1 billion purchase of long principals was also linked to speculation that fund managers were extending durations and possibly re-allocating assets out of stocks, analysts and traders said.
"You can imply from the market action that there is a lot of hedging against pre-payment risk in the mortgage market," another debt futures floor source said.
Traders said there was speculation in the last week that many mortgage holders may consider re-financing loans due to the steady decline in yields on the 30-year T-bond and 10-year T-note.

The U.S. June consumer price index, which rose 0.1 percent in both the overall and core rates, and U.S. June industrial production and capacity utilization data strengthened sentiment that price pressures were tame.
As a result, the data allayed concerns that U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan would make hawkish comments in next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress, they said.
Greenspan speaks on Thursday at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT to a House subcommittee on the Financial Services Competition Act.
Traders said T-bond futures were also jerked higher by heavy buying of T-bond call options. One U.S. bank bought 15,000 August 115-00 T-bond calls, as well as 5,000 10-year T-note options.

Locals, many of whom were caught short below the 114-14/32 to 114-15/32 area, were forced to cover once the options activity filtered into the futures pit. September T-bonds soared through 114-16/32, which was equivalent to 6.50 percent, and caught another wave of buying above 114-20/32.
Traders look for September T-bonds to test 115-03/32 in the near term.
December Eurodollars inched up to 94.08, but most of pit activity was confined in the deferred contracts, traders said.
One local commission house sold 8,000 red June Eurodollars and bought 8,000 red September contracts.

At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds were 24/32 higher at 114-22/32, 10-year notes were up 12/32 at 109-26/32, and December Eurodollars were up 0.025 basis point at 94.065. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
